findings.title: Invalid ERB close tag prevents the embed view from rendering
findings.body: The template opens a normal `if @topic_view.posts.present?` at line 2 and closes it with `<%- end if %>`. ERB compiles that to Ruby `end if`, which is not valid syntax. Any request that renders `embed/best` raises a SyntaxError, so the embedded comments never display. It should be `<%- end %>`.

findings.title: Imported feed content is stored as unsanitized raw HTML
findings.body: `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: raw_html`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged for that mode. `Jobs::PollFeed` feeds `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content)` into this path, so an RSS/Atom item containing encoded markup such as `<script>...</script>` is stored and later rendered with `raw post.cooked`; the script executes in the forum/embed origin. Remote feed content is not trusted; it must be sanitized/allowlisted before being stored as raw HTML, or this path must not use `raw_html`.

findings.title: Embed URL is interpolated into raw HTML without escaping
findings.body: The imported URL is inserted directly into a single-quoted href and link text: `#{url}`, and this content is saved as raw HTML. A URL containing a single quote or `<` (the only validation is that it starts with http:// or https://) can break out and inject arbitrary HTML/JS into the post. Escape `url` for HTML before building the link.

findings.title: Kernel#open on a caller-supplied URL can execute shell commands
findings.body: `import_remote` calls `open(url).read` on a URL supplied by callers. Ruby's `Kernel#open` executes a command when the filename starts with `|`; the Disqus importer passes `t[:link]` from the XML export directly into this method with no scheme validation, so a malicious export can run arbitrary shell commands when the importer is executed. Validate the URL scheme/host and use a non-command-opening HTTP API, or at least reject pipe and non-http URLs.

findings.title: PollFeed assumes every feed item has content and aborts on common RSS feeds
findings.body: `PollFeed` assumes every item has `i.content`; RSS 2.0 commonly exposes the body as `description`, and Atom items may use `summary`, so `i.content` can be nil. `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError, aborting `poll_feed` for all items. Since this job has `retry: false`, a single item without `content` prevents the feed from being imported. Use nil-safe fallback fields and handle failures per item.

findings.title: Protocol-relative URLs are rewritten to the source host
findings.body: The absolutization only handles paths beginning with `/` by stripping all leading slashes and prefixing the source host. For a protocol-relative URL such as `//cdn.example.com/image.png`, it produces `http://sourcehost/cdn.example.com/image.png` instead of `http://cdn.example.com/image.png`, breaking embedded images and links. Treat URLs beginning with `//` as protocol-relative and use the source scheme.

findings.title: Origin check accepts any origin that is a substring of discourseUrl
findings.body: The check `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` tests whether the origin is a substring of `discourseUrl`, not whether it matches the expected origin. For example, if `discourseUrl` is `http://example.com`, a message from `http://example.co` is accepted because that string is a prefix. Any page that can post to this window and has a matching substring origin can forge resize messages. Compare `e.origin` exactly to the parsed origin of `discourseUrl`.

findings.title: PollFeed setting tests short-circuit on feed_polling_enabled
findings.body: The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' examples only stub the one setting to nil but leave `feed_polling_enabled?` at its default false, so the first condition short-circuits and `poll_feed` is never called regardless of the setting under test. These specs would pass even if the URL/username checks were broken. Stub the other conditions true in each example.
